_meta.title: Meld — Ableton Live 12's bi-timbral dual macro-oscillator MPE synth
_meta.confidence_legend: CONFIRMED = primary/authoritative; LIKELY = strong secondary/single good source; UNCERTAIN = thin/contradicted/inference
_meta.note: Meld is a 2024 device with no confirmed artist-track canon. Every Section 3/4 track illustrates a TECHNIQUE, not Meld usage; flagged as such.

meld_is_bitimbral_macro_osc.claim: Meld is a bi-timbral, dual macro-oscillator, MPE-capable synthesizer with two independent engines (A and B), each with its own oscillator, filter, envelopes, LFOs, and MIDI/MPE modulation matrix.
meld_is_bitimbral_macro_osc.source: Ableton Reference Manual — Live Instrument Reference
meld_is_bitimbral_macro_osc.quote: Each of the device's engines has a dedicated filter, envelopes, LFOs, and a MIDI and MPE-enabled Modulation Matrix.

meld_bitimbral_definition.claim: Bi-timbral means the two engines produce, sculpt and combine two complete sounds independently.
meld_bitimbral_definition.source: Ableton blog — Meld: A Look at Live 12's New Bi-Timbral Synth
meld_bitimbral_definition.quote: Meld is bi-timbral, meaning its distinct engines can produce, sculpt and combine two complete sounds without being tied to the amplitude and filter envelopes of one system.

meld_NOT_physical_modeller.claim: CORRECTION: Meld is NOT a physical-modelling (Karplus-Strong/waveguide) synth. It is a macro-oscillator synth; only the Plate/Membrane Resonator FILTERS are physical-modelling-flavoured (modal). The 'Physical Modelling Hybrid' subtitle is inaccurate and should be changed.
meld_NOT_physical_modeller.source: Ableton DSP reference (osc list) + SOS (resonator filters) + Ableton blog (macro-osc framing)
meld_NOT_physical_modeller.quote: Scale-aware plate and membrane resonators that snap those resonant frequencies into tune with your track. [Meld is described throughout as a bi-timbral macro oscillator synth, not a physical modeller.]

meld_version_12_0_not_12_1.claim: CORRECTION: Meld shipped in the initial Live 12.0 release on 5 March 2024 (with Roar and Granulator III), NOT in 12.1. The brief's '12.1' is wrong.
meld_version_12_0_not_12_1.source: Ableton blog 'Live 12 — coming March 5' + Engadget + MusicTech launch coverage
meld_version_12_0_not_12_1.quote: Live 12 was available at Ableton.com starting March 5, 2024 ... new devices such as Meld, Roar, and Granulator III. [Engadget: 'Meld is exclusively available in the Live 12 Suite edition.']

meld_chord_osc_added_12_2.claim: The Chord oscillator type (four sawtooth oscillators playing chords) was ADDED in Live 12.2 (11 June 2025) — the only Meld feature added after the 12.0 launch. So Meld has 24 osc types at 12.0 and 25 at 12.2+.
meld_chord_osc_added_12_2.quote: Added a new Chord oscillator type, which is comprised of four sawtooth oscillators that play a variety of chords. Added new Meld presets that feature the Chord oscillator.

meld_suite_only.claim: Meld is a Live 12 Suite-exclusive device (not in Intro or Standard).
meld_suite_only.quote: Meld (New in Live 12) appears exclusively under the Suite column; not available in Intro and Standard editions.

meld_design_team.claim: Meld was designed by concept lead / UX designer Christian Kleine with lead engineer Rob Tubb.
meld_design_team.source: Sound on Sound — Ableton Live: Meld
meld_design_team.quote: Concept lead and UX designer: Christian Kleine. Lead engineer: Rob Tubb.

kleine_two_synths_quote.claim: Christian Kleine describes Meld as two synthesizers in one.
kleine_two_synths_quote.source: Sound on Sound — Ableton Live: Meld
kleine_two_synths_quote.quote: It's two synthesizers in one. It allows for a combination of two things, and this makes the sum bigger than its parts.

tubb_modular_influence_quote.claim: Rob Tubb cites Mutable Instruments / modular adaptability as a big influence on Meld.
tubb_modular_influence_quote.source: Sound on Sound — Ableton Live: Meld
tubb_modular_influence_quote.quote: The sheer adaptability and multi-function stuff that modules can do, that was a big influence.

kleine_scale_aware_quote.claim: Kleine considers scale awareness a must-have for any modern synth.
kleine_scale_aware_quote.source: Sound on Sound — Ableton Live: Meld
kleine_scale_aware_quote.quote: Even if you don't use scale awareness, this is a feature that I think is a must-have for any modern synth.

meld_24_osc_types_6_scale_aware.claim: Each engine offers twenty-four oscillator types including six scale-aware oscillators (marked with flat-sharp symbol).
meld_24_osc_types_6_scale_aware.source: Ableton Reference Manual — Live Instrument Reference
meld_24_osc_types_6_scale_aware.quote: Engines A and B each have a selection of twenty-four oscillator types to choose from, including six scale aware oscillators.

meld_osc_type_full_list.claim: The 24 oscillator types with their two macros each: Basic Shapes (Shape/Tone), Bitgrunge (Frequency/Mult), Bubble (Density/Spread), Chip (Tone/Rate), Crackle (Density/Intensity), Dual Basic Shapes (Shape/Detune), Extratone (Pitch/Env Amount), Filtered Noise (Frequency/Narrowness), Fold FM (FM Amount/Shape), Harmonic FM (FM Amount/FM Ratio), Noise Loop (Rate/Fade), Noisy Shapes (Shape/Rough), Rain (Tone/Rate), Shepard's Pi (Rate/Width), Simple FM (FM Amount/FM Ratio), Square 5th (5th Amount/Pulse Width), Square Sync (Freq 1/Freq 2), FM Bass aka Squelch (FM Amount/Feedback), Sub (Tone/Aux), Swarm Saw/Sine/Square/Triangle (Motion/Spacing), Tarp (Decay/Tone).
meld_osc_type_full_list.quote: Bitgrunge: A pseudo-random lo-fi square wave oscillator reminiscent of loading an old computer game from a tape. Shepard's Pi: A Shepard tone oscillator with depth and direction. Harmonic FM: A harmonic FM oscillator with modulation ratio and amount. FM Bass (Squelch): A FM oscillator with modulation index amount and operator feedback. [Full 24-entry table with per-type Macro 1 / Macro 2 enumerated.]

meld_six_scale_aware_named.claim: The six scale-aware oscillator types are Dual Basic Shapes, Chip, Swarm Sine, Swarm Triangle, Swarm Saw, and Swarm Square.
meld_six_scale_aware_named.source: Ableton Reference Manual — Live Instrument Reference
meld_six_scale_aware_named.quote: Six oscillator types support scale awareness: Dual Basic Shapes, Swarm Sine, Swarm Triangle, Swarm Saw, Swarm Square, and Chip.

meld_two_macros_per_osc.claim: Each oscillator type has exactly two dedicated macro knobs whose meaning changes with the selected type.
meld_two_macros_per_osc.quote: Each engine features two dedicated macro knobs, which change along with the oscillator type selected.

meld_squelch_feedback.claim: The FM Bass (Squelch) oscillator exposes operator feedback as its second macro — the one place Meld exposes FM feedback.
meld_squelch_feedback.quote: FM Bass (Squelch): A FM oscillator with modulation index amount and operator feedback. [Macro 1: FM Amount, Macro 2: Feedback]

meld_17_filter_types.claim: Each engine has one dedicated filter offering seventeen filter types (LP/HP/BP, phasers, comb, vocal/vowel formant, lo-fi/bitcrusher, resonators), each with two macro knobs.
meld_17_filter_types.source: MusicRadar — Ultimate guide to Meld + SOS
meld_17_filter_types.quote: 17 types available [filter examples: Plate Resonator, Phaser, Vowel filter, Lo-fi effects, Bitcrusher].

meld_resonator_filters_scale_aware.claim: The Plate Resonator and Membrane Resonator filters are scale-aware modal resonators that snap resonant frequencies to the track's tuning — the one genuinely physical-modelling-flavoured DSP element in Meld.
meld_resonator_filters_scale_aware.source: Sound on Sound — Ableton Live: Meld
meld_resonator_filters_scale_aware.quote: Scale-aware plate and membrane resonators that snap those resonant frequencies into tune with your track.

meld_envelopes_loop_modes.claim: Each engine has two envelopes (Amplitude + Modulation), ADSR with adjustable slopes and three loop modes: Trigger, Loop, and AD Loop. A Link Envelopes button links each engine's amp and mod envelopes.
meld_envelopes_loop_modes.source: Ableton Reference Manual — Live Instrument Reference
meld_envelopes_loop_modes.quote: Attack, Decay, Sustain, and Release, with slope adjustments and three loop modes: Trigger mode, Loop mode, and AD Loop mode. Link Envelopes button links each engine's Amplitude and Modulation envelopes.

meld_lfo_config.claim: Each engine has LFO 1 (with an FX panel), LFO 1 FX (eighteen effect types incl. S&H/fade-in, usable as an independent source), and LFO 2 (six classic waveforms). LFO 1 and LFO 1 FX are independent matrix sources.
meld_lfo_config.source: Ableton Reference Manual — Live Instrument Reference
meld_lfo_config.quote: LFO 1 (with FX panel for serial effects), LFO 1 FX (eighteen effect types), and LFO 2 (six classic waveforms). LFO 1 and LFO1 FX can be used as independent modulation sources in Meld's Modulation Matrix.

meld_lfo_200hz_audio_rate.claim: Meld's LFO rate reaches ~200 Hz, into audio rate, for tonal/sideband modulation effects.
meld_lfo_200hz_audio_rate.source: Sound on Sound — Ableton Live: Meld
meld_lfo_200hz_audio_rate.quote: LFO rate goes up to a relatively fast 200Hz, allowing you to achieve real audio-rate tonal effects by modulating volume or filter with LFO 1 FX.

meld_mod_matrix.claim: Each engine has its own Modulation Matrix (sources across top, targets down side, bipolar amounts), ~23 targets in expanded view, with cross-engine modulation (one engine's LFOs/envelopes can modulate the other engine).
meld_mod_matrix.source: Ableton Reference Manual + MusicRadar (~23 targets) + SOS (cross-engine)
meld_mod_matrix.quote: Meld's Modulation Matrix lets you assign modulation sources to modulation targets within the device. [MusicRadar: 'approximately 23 targets in expanded view'; SOS: 'Synth A's LFOs can modulate Synth B's parameters.']

meld_midi_mpe_sources.claim: Matrix MIDI sources include Velocity, Pitch (note), Random, Pitch Bend, Press (channel aftertouch), Modulation Wheel; MPE sources include per-note Note Pitch Bend, Slide (Y/CC74), and Press (per-note pressure).
meld_midi_mpe_sources.source: Ableton Reference Manual — Live Instrument Reference
meld_midi_mpe_sources.quote: Velocity, Pitch, Random, Pitch Bend, Press, Modulation Wheel, and MPE controls (Note Pitch Bend, Slide, and Press).

meld_mpe_designed_in.claim: Meld is designed MPE-first; the MIDI and MPE tabs turn MPE functionality into modulation sources, making Meld a dynamic performance tool.
meld_mpe_designed_in.source: Ableton — Meld pack page + Ableton blog
meld_mpe_designed_in.quote: Live's new MPE-capable synthesizer is designed for sound variety, playfulness and character. [Blog: 'Meld's MIDI and MPE tabs let you use MIDI and MPE functionality as modulation sources, which can turn Meld into an extremely dynamic performance tool.']

meld_mixer_global.claim: Per-engine mixer: Volume, Pan, Tone Filter (high/low tone cut). Global: Drive, Limiter, Master Volume. Voicing: Poly/Mono, glide modes Portamento and Glissando, Stacked Voices + Spread (unison), phase-reset options.
meld_mixer_global.quote: Per-engine: Volume, Pan, Tone Filter. Global controls include Drive, Limiter, Master Volume. Supports glide modes (Portamento and Glissando) and phase reset options. [MusicRadar: 'high/low tone cut in mixer section.']

meld_voice_cap_unresolved.claim: Polyphony cap is UNRESOLVED in public docs: one manual read says up to 32 voices, another says the Poly drop-down maxes at 12. VERIFY in the live device before stating a number on-mic.
meld_voice_cap_unresolved.quote: Supports up to 32 voices [one read] / Poly drop-down lets you increase voices up to 12 [another read]. CONFLICT — verify in device.

macro_oscillator_definition.claim: A macro-oscillator is a single oscillator slot hiding a complex DSP algorithm behind a small fixed set of high-level macros (two in Meld), trading fine editability for instant breadth and playability.
macro_oscillator_definition.source: Ableton — Meld pack page (macro framing) + Ableton DSP reference (per-type macros)
macro_oscillator_definition.quote: Each engine features two dedicated macro knobs, which change along with the oscillator type selected.

plaits_lineage.claim: The macro-oscillator-as-product idea was crystallized by Mutable Instruments (Émilie Gillet): Braids (2013), Plaits (2018, 16 synthesis models). Plaits' firmware/DSP was released open-source (MIT) and propagated to Behringer Brains, Arturia MicroFreak, VCV Rack, etc.
plaits_lineage.quote: Plaits contains 16 total synthesis engines [pitched + noise/percussion]. [SynthAnatomy: 'Behringer Brains, macro oscillator with 15 Mutable Instruments Plaits algorithms'; firmware released under permissive open source licenses.]

plaits_has_physical_models.claim: Plaits genuinely contains physical-modelling engines — Karplus-Strong (extended) and a modal resonator — which is the likely origin of the 'physical modelling' association; Meld inherited only the modal-resonator idea (as filters), not a Karplus-Strong oscillator.
plaits_has_physical_models.quote: Karplus-Strong ... excited by bursts of white noise. Modal resonator ... excited by a mallet or dust noise. [These are explicitly physical-modelling based.]

meld_plaits_influence_not_code.claim: Meld is acknowledged as influenced by Mutable/modular thinking (Tubb quote), but NO source documents Plaits open-source code being inside Meld. Frame as lineage/influence, never 'Plaits inside Meld.'
meld_plaits_influence_not_code.source: Sound on Sound — Ableton Live: Meld (Tubb influence quote)
meld_plaits_influence_not_code.quote: The sheer adaptability and multi-function stuff that modules can do, that was a big influence. [No claim of code reuse exists in any source consulted.]

mpe_paradigm.claim: MPE (MIDI Polyphonic Expression, MMA-adopted 2018) gives each note its own MIDI channel so pitch bend, a Y-axis Slide (CC74), and per-note pressure can be controlled independently per finger — popularized by ROLI Seaboard, LinnStrument, Push 3.
mpe_paradigm.source: General MIDI standard knowledge (flagged as such in dossier)
mpe_paradigm.quote: MPE controls (Note Pitch Bend, Slide, and Press) [as per-note matrix sources in Meld]. [MPE per-note-channel definition is general MIDI knowledge.]

aphex_per_note_iridium.claim: Aphex Twin collaborated on the Waldorf Iridium MK2 Per-Note Parameter Locks — illustrating the IDM per-note-timbre obsession that MPE in Meld serves. THEMATIC KINSHIP ONLY: no source links Aphex to Meld.
aphex_per_note_iridium.source: MusicRadar — Waldorf Iridium Aphex Twin collaboration
aphex_per_note_iridium.quote: the result of a collaboration with legendary Aphex Twin [Per-Note Parameter Locks]. NOTE: connects Aphex to per-note control as an idea, NOT to Meld.

autechre_modulate_not_notes.claim: Autechre's self-generating-pattern / modulate-a-parameter aesthetic (custom Max/MSP from Confield on) is an aesthetic analogue for Meld's loop-mode Mod-Env -> oscillator-macro trick. Aesthetic kinship; UNVERIFIED as Meld usage.
autechre_modulate_not_notes.source: Sound on Sound — Autechre: Techno Logical
autechre_modulate_not_notes.quote: [Autechre's documented custom Max/MSP, parameter-driven self-generating approach. No Meld usage claim.]

squarepusher_builds_own.claim: Squarepusher builds his own tools in Reaktor and avoids off-the-shelf presets — used as an honest negative; no Meld usage claimed.
squarepusher_builds_own.quote: [Squarepusher's documented preference for self-built Reaktor instruments over off-the-shelf devices.]

plaid_polymer_texture.claim: Plaid's Polymer (2019) used Tone2 Icarus + Madrona Polymer for scanning/morphing textures — used as the 'timbre-as-composition' technique exemplar, NOT a Plaits/Meld claim.
plaid_polymer_texture.quote: more original sounds perhaps were made with Tone2's Icarus using the 3D Wavetable functionality ... making and scanning through wavetables on Polymer.

boc_analog_texture.claim: Boards of Canada use analog gear + sampler (Akai S1000) for their field-recording-flavoured texture — cited as an aesthetic target for Meld's Rain/Crackle oscillators, NOT a Meld claim (and confirmed they do not use Meld-style wavetable/macro synths).
boc_analog_texture.quote: [BoC's documented analog + Akai S1000 sampler setup. Used as texture target, not Meld usage.]

live_12_release_date.source: Ableton blog — Live 12 coming March 5 + DJ Life
live_12_release_date.quote: Live 12 was available at Ableton.com starting March 5, 2024.
